target_route: NAD+ precursor -> SIRT2 -> deacetylated BubR1 K668 -> reduced BubR1 turnover
drug_class_examples: NAD+ precursors (nicotinamide riboside, nicotinamide mononucleotide, niacin)
regulatory_status: niacin is an approved drug; NR and NMN are marketed as supplements, not approved drugs
rationale: The only route identified that acts on BubR1 abundance itself rather than downstream of it. SIRT2 deacetylates BubR1 at K668 and opposes its degradation; NAD+ repletion raises BubR1 in vivo and SIRT2 overexpression extends lifespan in BubR1-hypomorphic mice (24825348). The dosage logic is supported in both directions: reduced BubR1 produces aneuploidy and progeroid phenotypes (15208629), increased BubR1 protects against aneuploidy and cancer (23242215). K668 lies outside both patient alleles, and the stop-gain allele is predicted to undergo NMD, so the missense-derived protein is the plausible substrate.
key_limitations: No MVA-specific in vivo test of NAD+ repletion exists; all BubR1 evidence is murine. The K668 argument is inferred from domain position, not experimentally shown for N1016K. NAD+ availability also supports proliferating tumour metabolism, and rhabdomyosarcoma cells depend on the FoxM1/BUB1B axis (23002205), so the direction of effect in a cancer-predisposition background is unresolved and must be tested before any translational claim.
proposed_experiment: In patient-derived and isogenic BUB1B-mutant cells, measure BubR1 protein by immunoblot and K668 acetylation by IP-MS under vehicle vs NAD+ precursor; read out micronuclei, chromosome missegregation and aneuploidy by karyotyping. Run matched assays in RMS lines to test whether the same exposure increases proliferation (distinguishing phenotypic rescue from a proliferative effect).

target_route: senescent-cell survival network (SRC/ABL/ephrin kinases, BCL-xL/PI3K nodes) -> apoptosis of senescent cells
drug_class_examples: senolytic combinations studied as dasatinib plus quercetin; fisetin
regulatory_status: dasatinib is approved including in paediatric haematological indications; quercetin and fisetin are supplements
rationale: Addresses the senescence arm of BubR1 biology rather than the mitotic arm. BubR1-hypomorphic mice accumulate p16-positive senescent cells, and genetic clearance of those cells delayed sarcopenia and other degenerative phenotypes in exactly that model (22048312) - unusually direct model-to-mechanism correspondence. Senolytic compounds were derived from the pro-survival network of senescent cells (25754370) and have been given intermittently to humans in early-phase trials (31542391).
key_limitations: Evidence is for genetic clearance in mice, not pharmacological senolysis in MVA. Senescence is also a tumour-suppressive program, so removing senescent cells in a cancer-predisposition background is mechanistically ambiguous. Human senolytic data are early-phase, in adults, and in other diseases. This hypothesis targets a downstream consequence and does not correct the BubR1 defect.
proposed_experiment: Quantify senescence burden (p16/p21, SA-beta-gal, SASP cytokines) in BUB1B-mutant vs control primary cells; test whether intermittent senolytic exposure selectively depletes senescent cells without affecting proliferating controls. In BubR1-hypomorphic mice, compare pharmacological senolysis with the published genetic clearance readouts, with tumour incidence as a co-primary endpoint.

target_route: beta-tubulin -> spindle poisons require a competent SAC to arrest cells
drug_class_examples: vinca alkaloids and taxanes (agents already standard in rhabdomyosarcoma protocols)
rationale: Not a repurposing proposal but a mechanism-derived research question that the same analysis surfaces. Spindle poisons kill by triggering a SAC-dependent mitotic arrest; cells with a weakened checkpoint are reported to resist them and to slip through mitosis. A published MVA case was managed with reduced-intensity chemotherapy (31184400), and genomic-instability syndromes are recognised as a group in which anticancer treatment sensitivity differs (39264246). Because BUB1B-related MVA combines a weakened SAC with high embryonal tumour risk (15475955), the interaction between genotype and spindle-poison response is a testable question of direct relevance to this gene.
key_limitations: The resistance literature is largely from cancer cell lines with acquired checkpoint attenuation, not from constitutional biallelic BUB1B deficiency; direction and magnitude in that setting are unknown. The MVA chemotherapy literature consists of isolated case reports with no comparative data. Any clinical interpretation is outside the scope of this analysis and belongs to the treating oncology team.
proposed_experiment: Measure mitotic arrest duration (live-cell imaging), slippage frequency and viability in BUB1B-mutant vs isogenic control cells across a dose range of a vinca alkaloid and a taxane, to establish whether checkpoint status shifts the dose-response curve and in which direction.

target_route: APC/C-CDC20 -> restore mitotic delay lost with BubR1
drug_class_examples: proTAME, apcin (tool compounds; no approved CDC20/APC-C inhibitor)
regulatory_status: not approved; preclinical tool compounds only
rationale: Retained explicitly as a negative result. Mechanistically this is the most direct downstream compensation for a failed MCC, and the Step 2 analysis ranked it highly, but the Step 3 mapping found no approved drug against CDC20, ANAPC2 or UBE2C in any direction. Reported rescue of segregation errors by low-dose APC/C antagonism is preclinical only.
key_limitations: No approved drug exists, so this cannot satisfy a repurposing brief. The procedure explicitly flags APC/C-CDC20 inhibition as a hypothesis rather than an established strategy, and deliberately slowing mitosis genome-wide carries its own theoretical liabilities. Documented so the gap is visible rather than silently dropped.
proposed_experiment: n/a - reported as a druggability gap; would require tool-compound characterisation in BUB1B-mutant cells before any translational framing.

target_route: proteotoxic and metabolic dependencies of aneuploid cells (proteasome, DHODH, HSP90)
rationale: Included for completeness because Step 3 found genuinely approved, direction-concordant drugs here, unlike most of the panel. Aneuploid cells carry proteotoxic and metabolic burdens that create selective vulnerabilities (21315436).
key_limitations: Mechanistically the most distant from the BUB1B defect: it targets the aneuploid state generally, not BubR1 function, and would act on constitutionally aneuploid tissue rather than correcting anything. Selective toxicity against a patient's own somatic cells is the opposite of phenotypic rescue, which is why this scores lowest on mechanistic relevance despite the best drug availability. Listed as a research direction, not a prioritised hypothesis.
proposed_experiment: Compare aneuploid vs euploid isogenic lines for differential sensitivity, explicitly reporting the therapeutic window and distinguishing selective toxicity from rescue.
